negatives.observed: The first post-x1 four-way equality wrapper embedded an ancestry command inside a PowerShell hash literal and failed at parse time.
negatives.recovery: Captured the ancestry exit code before constructing the receipt and then proved clean local, upstream, tracking, and live-remote equality.
negatives.promotion_effect: The failed wrapper is not equality evidence and closed no gate.

negatives.observed: The first inherited tool-size inventory piped directly from a foreach block and PowerShell rejected the empty pipe element.
negatives.recovery: Collected the rows in a variable and formatted the completed inventory separately.
negatives.promotion_effect: The parser failure is retained and is not a tool-inventory pass.

negatives.observed: A broad inherited evidence-file chunk read exceeded its bounded timeout before returning the requested section.
negatives.recovery: Used targeted searches and smaller bounded reads to identify the proposal-specific and validation surfaces.
negatives.promotion_effect: The timed-out read is retained and is not completeness evidence.

negatives.observed: The first stale-label search used an unterminated PowerShell double-quoted pattern and stopped before scanning.
negatives.recovery: Reran the read-only search with a literal single-quoted pattern and obtained the complete targeted result.
negatives.promotion_effect: The parser failure is retained and is not stale-label evidence.

negatives.observed: A combined evidence-builder patch could not match an encoding-sensitive context block and applied no changes.
negatives.recovery: Split the edit into bounded patches using UTF-8-inspected context and verified each applied hunk.
negatives.promotion_effect: The rejected patch changed no evidence and is not an implementation pass.

negatives.observed: The first static-report patch used a mojibake rendering of characters that were already valid UTF-8 and matched no lines.
negatives.recovery: Read the source explicitly as UTF-8 and patched only the stale GMUT summary text.
negatives.promotion_effect: The no-op patch is retained and is not report validation evidence.

negatives.observed: The combined evidence-snapshot materialization exceeded its first bounded timeout after fully creating evidence-A but before creating evidence-B.
negatives.recovery: Verified evidence-A directly and created evidence-B separately with an extended bounded window.
negatives.promotion_effect: The timed-out combined operation is retained and is not a two-snapshot validation pass.

negatives.observed: A broad post-timeout worktree inventory and state wrapper exceeded its bounded timeout without returning a receipt.
negatives.recovery: Used path-scoped existence and exact detached-state checks instead of a broad worktree listing.
negatives.promotion_effect: The timed-out inventory is retained and is not snapshot-state evidence.

negatives.observed: The first evidence-A state wrapper called Trim on the null branch name expected from a detached worktree.
negatives.recovery: Switched to null-safe output handling and kept detached branch output empty by design.
negatives.promotion_effect: The wrapper failure is retained and is not detached-state evidence.

negatives.observed: A second evidence-A state wrapper still attempted Trim on an empty pipeline value and failed before producing a receipt.
negatives.recovery: Used Out-String before trimming and then proved exact head, detached state, and clean status.
negatives.promotion_effect: The second wrapper failure is retained and is not snapshot-state evidence.

negatives.observed: The first closeout-snapshot command used an inferred full commit hash, and Git rejected the invalid reference before creating a worktree.
negatives.recovery: Read the exact full commit from Git, confirmed the target path was still absent, and created a fresh detached closeout snapshot at that exact revision.
negatives.promotion_effect: The invalid-reference attempt changed no repository state and is not snapshot evidence.
